# Sirach Chapter 36 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 36 | **Agents Consulted:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA

---

## Council Notes

Chapter 36 divides sharply into two: a communal prayer for national deliverance (vv. 1–17) and a series of reflections on discernment and marriage (vv. 18–26). The prayer (sometimes called Ben Sira's "Nationalistic Prayer") is the most overtly political passage in the book, calling on God to crush foreign rulers and restore Israel's scattered tribes. The verb "magnified" in v. 4 echoes the Kaddish. Verse 10 — "rulers who say, There is no one but us" — is clearly a reference to Seleucid imperial ideology. The transition at v. 18 is jarring: domestic analogies (palate, wife) follow war poetry. This is intentional literary arrangement. The wife sections (vv. 21–26) must be rendered accurately as reflections of their ancient context; the "pillar of support" image (v. 24) is architectural and dignified.

---

**36:1** Have mercy on us, O Lord, God of all, and look upon us,

**36:2** and cast your terror upon all the nations.

**36:3** Raise your hand against foreign peoples and let them see your might.

**36:4** As you have been shown holy among us before them, so be magnified among them before our eyes;

**36:5** and let them acknowledge you as we have acknowledged you, that there is no God but you, O Lord.

**36:6** Renew your signs and work further wonders; make glorious your hand and your right arm.

**36:7** Rouse your wrath and pour out fury; destroy the adversary and wipe out the enemy.

**36:8** Hasten the time and remember your sworn oath, and let people recount your mighty acts.

**36:9** Let fiery wrath consume the survivor, and let those who abuse your people find destruction.

**36:10** Crush the heads of hostile rulers who say, "There is no one but ourselves."

**36:11** Gather together all the tribes of Jacob, and restore them to their inheritance as in the beginning.

**36:12** Have mercy, O Lord, on the people called by your name, on Israel, whom you named firstborn.

**36:13** Have compassion on your holy city, Jerusalem, the place of your rest.

**36:14** Fill Zion with the proclamation of your deeds, and your temple with your glory.

**36:15** Bear witness on behalf of those you created from the beginning, and bring to fulfillment the prophecies spoken in your name.

**36:16** Reward those who wait for you, and let your prophets prove trustworthy.

**36:17** Hear the prayer of your servants, according to the blessing of Aaron over your people, that all who live on the earth may know that you are the Lord, the eternal God.

**36:18** The belly accepts any kind of food, yet one food is better than another.

**36:19** The palate distinguishes between kinds of game, and a discerning mind detects false speech.

**36:20** A perverse heart causes grief, but a person of experience can pay back in kind.

**36:21** A woman will accept any man, yet one woman is better than another.

**36:22** A woman's beauty makes a man's face light up; there is nothing more desirable than this.

**36:23** If in addition there is kindness and gentleness on her tongue, then her husband is not like other men.

**36:24** Whoever acquires a wife acquires his finest possession — a helper suited to him and a pillar of support.

**36:25** Where there is no fence, property is stripped bare; and where there is no wife, a man wanders and sighs.

**36:26** Who will trust an agile robber who slips from city to city? So who will trust a man who has no home and lodges wherever night overtakes him?
